stemMd: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Belmont found that a mesh coarse enough to let air through collects more fog water than the finest possible weave.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Belmont gave up on mesh nets altogether once she found that the fog was being pushed around them rather than through them.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Fog rolls inland over the hills above Cerro Alto on most mornings, even though the coastal town receives almost no rain.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The main obstacle to collecting fog water at Cerro Alto is that thick fog reaches the ridge on only a few mornings each year.

explanationMd:
The main idea is the point the whole passage is built to make, so it has to cover the passage's turn: the expectation Belmont started from, and the result that overturned it.

The passage moves in three steps. It describes the nets, reports that Belmont chose a very fine weave because she expected a denser mesh to intercept more droplets, and then reports that the fine nets did worst while a coarser mesh yielded nearly three times as much water. The option about a coarser mesh outperforming the finest possible weave is the only one that carries that reversal.

A quick way to check a main-idea answer is to ask whether the passage would still need its last three sentences if the option were true. The option about fog arriving on most mornings is a true detail from the first sentence, but the passage does not exist to tell you about the weather; everything after sentence one would be surplus. The options about abandoning the nets and about fog being rare are not supported at all.

distractorRationale.b: The passage never says Belmont gave up on nets. Air being pushed around the fine weave is the reason the fine nets failed, and her response was a coarser mesh, not abandonment of the method.
distractorRationale.d: This contradicts the first sentence, which says thick fog rolls inland on most mornings, not on only a few mornings a year. The scarcity at Cerro Alto is rain, not fog, which is exactly why fog collection is worth trying there.
distractorRationale.c: This is an accurate detail, but it is the passage's setting rather than its point. A main idea has to account for the experiment and its surprising result, and this sentence says nothing about either.

accessibilityText: Using the passage about Nadia Belmont's fog-collecting mesh nets at Cerro Alto, choose the statement that best expresses the passage's main idea. The four choices say: that Belmont found a mesh coarse enough to let air through collects more fog water than the finest possible weave; that Belmont gave up on mesh nets altogether once she found the fog was being pushed around them rather than through them; that fog rolls inland over the hills above Cerro Alto on most mornings although the town receives almost no rain; and that the main obstacle to collecting fog water there is that thick fog reaches the ridge on only a few mornings each year.

provenance.notes: Original item. One distractor is a true detail from the passage, so the item turns on the difference between a supporting fact and the central claim.

review.author: digital-sat-wave4-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The central point is that the fine weave performed worst because air could not pass through it. A coarser mesh that slowed the air without blocking it yielded nearly three times as much water. A captures this. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave7-sat-rw-run1) reached the same answer: The text builds to the finding that the fine weave did worst and a coarser mesh that let air through gave nearly three times the water. B is contradicted, because she switched to a coarser mesh rather than giving up nets. C is only the setting. D contradicts 'fog rolls inland on most mornings'.]

review.notes: Author's own solve and uniqueness check: C is the only option covering the passage's reversal (fine mesh expected to be best, coarse mesh actually best). D is true but is setting, not the point; A and B contradict the text, so no second option is defensible. Not published: awaiting a blind independent solve by a second party. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key. v2: choices rebalanced so the key no longer stands out by length, detail or hedging (answer-length cue found by tmp/cue-scan.mjs); stem, passage and key unchanged; re-solved blind.
